title: Sunny and the Rain Puddles | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the Quokka discovers a string of shallow puddles left by the afternoon rain and finds that each one holds a perfect upside-down reflection of the moonlit sky. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
The puddles were everywhere.

The afternoon rain had filled every low place in the path — small round pools that caught the moonlight and threw it back up at the sky. Sunny walked slowly, stepping around each one.

Then she stopped and looked into the nearest puddle.

There was a whole sky in there.

Not a reflection she expected — not a blurry, rippled approximation. A still, clear, perfect sky. Dark navy with stars. The moon, small and bright, sitting in the puddle just as it sat overhead. She moved her head and the reflected moon moved with her.

She looked up, then down. Sky. Puddle. Sky. Puddle.

Two skies.

She walked slowly along the puddle chain, looking into each one. Each puddle held a slightly different piece of sky. This one had more stars. That one had the edge of a cloud. The next one was so shallow the reflection shimmered when a moth flew past.

She crouched beside a particularly large puddle.

In it she could see her own face — round and soft — staring back up at her, surrounded by stars.

She waved.

The puddle-Sunny waved back.

She sat down at the edge of the puddle and looked at her starry reflection for a long time.

The moon in the puddle shone as brightly as the moon in the sky.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, rain puddles. Goodnight, little one.
